test_title: SSC Stenographer 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

That accident happened [A] /a long time ago, but [B] / I have shivered at [C] / the thought of it ever for [D].
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 
 
The error lies in part D – “the thought of it ever for” is grammatically incorrect.

 
 
• 
 
The expression “ever for” is not used in English. The word “ever” is generally used with “since” or “after” to express continuity of time from a particular event in the past up to the present.

 
 
• 
 
The correct phrase should therefore be “ever since”, meaning from that time until now.

 
 
• 
 
The sentence talks about a lasting emotional reaction — the speaker has continued to shiver whenever they think of the accident. To show this continued effect, the present perfect tense (“I have shivered”) must be followed by a phrase indicating continuity, i.e., “ever since.”

 
 
• 
 
Hence, the correct sentence will be:

 “That accident happened a long time ago, but I have shivered at the thought of it ever since.”

 
 
• 
 
This corrected version expresses that even though the accident occurred long ago, its emotional impact still remains with the speaker.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *“That accident happened a long time ago, but I have shivered at the thought of it ever since.”*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A:** “That accident happened” – grammatically correct, simple past tense used properly.
 
• **B:** “a long time ago, but” – correct use of a time expression and conjunction.
 
• **C:** “I have shivered at” – correct present perfect tense to indicate an ongoing feeling.
 
• **D:** “the thought of it ever for” – incorrect phrase; should be “ever since.”
